title: LLM-Generated GraphQL Mocks Arrive at Airbnb and Expedia, While the Spec Lags Behind
gist: Expedia open-sourced mockql-rs, a Rust CLI that generates GraphQL mock responses from an LLM at request time — the third incompatible attempt in six months after Airbnb's build-time @generateMock directive and a GraphQL Foundation RFC still at Stage 0 strawman with no champion; two of the three reuse the same @mock directive name to mean different things, and Expedia's merged responses give backend data and model output equal authority with nothing marking which is which.

themes.theme: Schema as the constraint that makes generation usable

insights.claim: The shared premise across all three GraphQL mocking approaches is that a selection set is already a specification, so the schema hands a model a bounded shape for free.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A transferable rule for deploying LLMs: supply the shape, let the model fill it — the inverse of open-ended generation that fails.
insights.quote: models are poor at inventing shapes and good at filling them in, and a schema hands them a bounded shape for free
insights.locator: The shared premise is that a GraphQL selection set

insights.claim: The author argues this pattern surfaced in GraphQL rather than REST specifically because schema-shaped output is what makes generated data usable rather than plausible-looking noise, and is also what lets tooling detect when generated data has stopped matching the query.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Predicts where LLM tooling lands next: typed, schema-bearing interfaces get automated first; untyped REST surfaces lag.
insights.quote: Schema-shaped output is exactly the constraint that makes generated data usable rather than plausible-looking noise
insights.locator: The more durable observation is why this pattern surfaced

insights.claim: The status quo being replaced is a developer hand-typing a two-hundred-line JSON fixture that the next morning's schema change invalidates.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Names the concrete cost being attacked — fixture maintenance — which sizes the addressable pain for mocking tooling.
insights.locator: The alternative, as his post describes it

themes.theme: Three incompatible designs, one directive name

insights.claim: Expedia's mockql-rs is a standalone Rust CLI sitting between client and server that parses and validates operations against the schema with apollo-compiler, splits @mock-annotated fields from real ones, forwards real fields upstream, prompts the model with the operation and a subset schema, then merges both into one response.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A proxy-shaped architecture means adoption requires no client library change — the lowest-friction distribution model for this class of tool.
insights.locator: mockql-rs sits between client and server

insights.claim: Expedia deliberately chose a CLI over an SDK on the grounds that any test runner, CI job or build script can execute a process, avoiding a client-library dependency.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: CLI-over-SDK is a repeatable packaging decision for polyglot enterprise environments where per-language SDKs multiply maintenance cost.
insights.quote: Expedia chose a CLI on the grounds that any test runner, CI job or build script can execute a process, avoiding an SDK or client-library dependency.
insights.locator: Expedia chose a CLI on the grounds

insights.claim: Airbnb's competing @generateMock directive published in April runs at build time inside Niobe code generation, emitting a JSON mock file plus typed accessor functions for demo apps, snapshot tests and unit tests, and deliberately preserves engineers' manual edits on regeneration.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Build-time generation with edit preservation is the design that keeps snapshot tests deterministic — the requirement Expedia's runtime approach cannot meet.

insights.claim: The GraphQL Foundation RFC defines @mock on operations rather than fields, with a name argument selecting between named responses, and requires a conforming client to return a mock without issuing any network request — mocks living in a __graphql_mocks__ directory with a reserved __default__ key.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: The spec's no-network requirement is architecturally incompatible with Expedia's merge-with-live-data proxy — these cannot converge without one side breaking.
insights.locator: The RFC takes a third position

insights.claim: Three public attempts at LLM-generated GraphQL mocks landed within six months — a February GraphQL Foundation RFC, Airbnb's April directive and Expedia's mockql-rs — arriving at markedly different designs with two reusing the same directive name for different semantics.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Rapid independent reinvention signals genuine demand but also predicts a standards fight and wasted integration effort.
insights.quote: It is the third public attempt in six months at the same problem

insights.claim: In Expedia's merged response the hotel name and address come from the backend while restaurant names, descriptions and distances are model output, yet both carry equal authority in the same payload and nothing marks which is which.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Unlabelled provenance in a shared payload is the failure mode to watch as LLM-generated data enters production data paths — a data-integrity and audit risk.
insights.quote: Both carry equal authority in the same payload, and nothing in the response marks which is which.
insights.locator: The hotel name and address came from the backend

insights.claim: Expedia's data is generated fresh on each run, which delivers contextual coherence but not the repeatability that snapshot tests depend on, and neither the Expedia nor Airbnb post addresses what non-deterministic fixtures mean for CI.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Non-determinism silently breaks the test-suite contract — the unresolved blocker to adopting runtime LLM mocking in CI.
insights.quote: Neither post addresses what non-deterministic fixtures mean for CI.
insights.locator: That difference matters more than the syntax

insights.claim: The RFC requires clients to detect when a mock response has drifted out of validity for its operation and force corrective action, and states mocks must be validated as part of the application test suite.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Drift detection is the discipline separating a governed mocking standard from ad-hoc generation — a checklist item when evaluating vendors.
insights.locator: The RFC requires clients to detect when a mock response

themes.theme: Standards risk and the agent workflow

insights.claim: The GraphQL RFC remains at Stage 0, described as a strawman with no champion listed — the earliest point in the specification process and no guarantee of progression — while Expedia's implementation already diverges on directive placement, argument name and network behaviour.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Adopting @mock today means betting on one vendor's reading of a name the spec also claims — a lock-in and rework risk teams should price explicitly.
insights.quote: a team standardising on @mock today is standardising on one vendor's reading of a name the specification also claims
insights.locator: For teams weighing adoption, the standards position is the caveat

insights.claim: The RFC anticipates the agent workflow directly by recommending implementers ship an Agent Skill with a suggested SKILL.md so coding agents can add or modify mock variants conversationally, placing mock management alongside other repository conventions agents are taught.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Specifications now shipping agent-facing artefacts is an early sign that agent-readability becomes a standards requirement, not an afterthought.
insights.locator: The RFC also anticipates the agent workflow directly

insights.claim: Whether LLM-generated GraphQL mocking becomes a specification or three incompatible implementations is currently an open question.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Fragmentation risk is unresolved — delay standardising internal tooling until a champion emerges for the RFC.
insights.quote: Whether that becomes a specification or three incompatible implementations is currently an open question.
